questions.question: Which entropy is the right quantity for one-shot guessing security of a key?
options: Shannon entropy H = -Σ p(x) log2 p(x)
questions.explanation: An adversary's best one-shot guess succeeds with probability max_x p(x). Min-entropy directly encodes that worst case; Shannon averages over the distribution and can overstate security.

questions.question: What is the Shannon entropy of a fair coin (in bits)?
How does the Rényi entropy H_α(X) behave as a function of α ≥ 0?
options: Monotone non-increasing in α: H_0 ≥ H_1 ≥ H_2 ≥ H_∞
Convex but not monotone in α
Constant in α for any fixed distribution
questions.explanation: Rényi entropy decreases as α grows. So min-entropy (α = ∞) is always the smallest of the named entropies.

questions.question: For the distribution `{a: 0.5, b: 0.25, c: 0.125, d: 0.125}`, what is the min-entropy?
questions.explanation: H_∞ = -log2(max p) = -log2(0.5) = 1 bit. (Shannon would give 1.75 — much more optimistic.)

questions.question: Which statement about KL divergence D(P || Q) is correct?
options: It is non-negative, asymmetric, and can be +∞ when Q(x)=0 < P(x) for some x
It is a metric satisfying D(P,Q) = D(Q,P) and the triangle inequality
It is bounded above by 1 for all P, Q
It equals the statistical distance between P and Q
questions.explanation: KL is non-negative (Gibbs) but asymmetric and unbounded; it is not a metric. It is connected to SD via Pinsker's inequality, not equal to it.

questions.question: Which formula correctly relates mutual information and entropy?
options: I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)
I(X; Y) = H(X | Y) + H(Y | X)
I(X; Y) = H(X, Y) - H(X) - H(Y)
questions.explanation: Mutual information is the gap between the joint entropy and the sum of marginal entropies; it equals 0 iff X and Y are independent.

questions.question: Leftover Hash Lemma rule of thumb: to extract L uniform bits at statistical security 2^-s from a source with min-entropy k, you need roughly:
questions.explanation: The LHL says L ≤ k - 2 log2(1/ε) with ε = 2^-s, giving k ≥ L + 2s. The factor 2 is why high-quality extractors lose entropy.

questions.question: A TRNG outputs each bit independently with Pr[bit = 0] = 0.9. What is the per-bit min-entropy?
questions.explanation: Min-entropy is -log2 max p = -log2 0.9 ≈ 0.152. Shannon (0.469) is the wrong quantity for guessing security.
